# Molar

> Molar is a beta browser automation and QA platform for web applications. Its QA workflows test customer journeys in a real browser; its platform also supports scoped browser tasks for people and AI agents.

This map is generated from crawlable canonical HTML pages. Product availability and coverage depend on the configured environment; the linked pages are the source of truth.

## Start here
- [Molar — AI QA for Web Apps & Third-Party Integrations](https://molar.it/) — AI agents that test your web app like a customer. Verify signup, payments, email and the services behind every click with Molar.

## Guides
- [AI agents and the future of software testing | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/ai-agents-future-software-testing) — A practical guide to verification loops for coding agents, with deterministic checks where judgment matters.
- [AI Playwright test generation: how it actually works in 2026 | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/ai-playwright-test-generation) — How AI Playwright test generation actually works — crawling, flow mapping, locator selection, self-healing, and CI export. A practical engineering guide with code.
- [API mocking vs stateful service clones | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/api-mocking-vs-service-clones) — Mocks stub responses; clones run stateful vendor semantics — webhooks included. When each is right.
- [Continuous testing in your CI/CD pipeline | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/continuous-testing-ci-cd-pipeline) — Where tests belong across commit, PR, deploy, and production — and what to run at each stage without killing velocity.
- [E2E testing best practices that survive scale | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/e2e-testing-best-practices) — A practical E2E playbook: test the critical path, user-visible selectors, deterministic data, fast feedback.
- [Email workflow testing: OTPs, invites, notifications | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/email-workflow-testing-otp) — Verify the whole email path in tests — delivery, links, codes — without SMTP or real inboxes. Deterministic and instant.
- [Flaky tests: root causes and durable fixes | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/flaky-tests-causes-and-fixes) — Why tests flake — timing, shared state, third parties, environments — and durable fixes for each. Stop re-running, start fixing.
- [Playwright in GitHub Actions: PR gating that holds | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/github-actions-playwright-ci) — Set up Playwright in GitHub Actions: caching, sharding, traces, required checks that block merges without drowning CI.
- [Playwright vs Cypress in 2026: an honest comparison | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/playwright-vs-cypress-comparison) — Architecture, multi-tab, iframes, debugging, CI scale, ecosystem. Where each wins — and how generated Playwright changes the math.
- [Regression testing strategies for fast-moving teams | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/regression-testing-strategies) — Full suites don't scale; skipping tests doesn't either. Risk-based selection, PR gates, and insurance runs that work.
- [Required status checks: a practical merge-gate guide | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/required-status-checks-merge-gate) — How to make failing checks actually block merges: branch protection, required checks, advisory vs required modes, escape hatches.
- [Self-healing test automation, done right | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/self-healing-test-automation) — How self-healing really works: locator re-ranking, intent capture, approval gates — and why silent rewrites mask real regressions.
- [Shift-left testing, explained for shipping teams | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/shift-left-testing-explained) — Catch bugs where they're cheapest — design and PR, not production. Practical shift-left without slowing reviews.
- [Staging environments are lying to you | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/staging-environment-alternatives) — Drift, dirty data, fake integrations. Why staging fails to predict production — and what to run against instead.
- [Startup QA without a QA team | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/startup-qa-without-qa-team) — You can't hire QA before PMF. Critical-path automation, PR gates, production guard — a lean playbook for founders.
- [Synthetic monitoring for production, beyond uptime pings | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/synthetic-monitoring-production) — Uptime pings miss broken flows. Synthetic checks walk critical paths every few minutes and catch what pings can't.
- [Test data management best practices | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/test-data-management-best-practices) — Deterministic IDs, seeded state, synthetic identities, PII hygiene. Test data rules that kill cross-test interference.
- [Test Stripe checkout without charging a real card | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/test-stripe-without-real-cards) — Test Stripe checkout and billing flows safely using stateful API clones. Isolated test charges, fewer test-mode gaps — deterministic Stripe clones in CI and production guard.
- [Testing Twilio SMS and OTP flows without real numbers | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/test-twilio-sms-otp-flows) — Real SMS is slow, costly, and flaky in CI. Stateful Twilio clones deliver OTPs instantly with deterministic codes.
- [Payment succeeded. Why is the account still locked? | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/testing-delayed-payment-webhooks-and-account-access) — A practical test plan for delayed payment webhooks, duplicate deliveries and the account access a paying customer expects.
- [Testing third-party APIs safely: Stripe, SendGrid, S3 | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/testing-third-party-apis-safely) — Sandbox limitations, rate limits, fake-data drift. Destruction-safe clones give tests real API semantics with zero blast radius.
- [Visual regression testing: a pragmatic guide | Molar](https://molar.it/blog/visual-regression-testing-guide) — Screenshot diffs that don't drown you in noise: scope, thresholds, baselines, and why semantic assertions come first.

## Products
- [Cartographer | Molar](https://molar.it/products/cartographer) — Turn a product URL and a user goal into browser evidence your team can inspect.
- [Clones | Molar](https://molar.it/products/clones) — Stateful local service doubles for the third parties your application depends on.
- [Guard | Molar](https://molar.it/products/guard) — Run release and production checks around the journeys your users depend on.
- [Mender | Molar](https://molar.it/products/mender) — A guarded repair workflow for investigating failures and preparing a proposed change.
- [Trace | Molar](https://molar.it/products/trace) — Inspect browser runs through structured evidence, screenshots, and replay oriented artifacts.

## Comparisons
- [Molar Guard vs Checkly | Molar](https://molar.it/vs/checkly) — Compare Molar Guard and Checkly. Guard gates PRs with affected-scenario E2E tests, runs safe production synthetics via Clones, and drafts fix PRs with Mender. Checkly focuses on Playwright synthetics and uptime.
- [Molar vs Cypress | Molar](https://molar.it/vs/cypress) — Compare Molar and Cypress. Molar authors and maintains critical-path tests autonomously, guards production, and clones third-party APIs. Cypress is a framework you write and maintain yourself.
- [Molar vs Playwright | Molar](https://molar.it/vs/playwright) — Compare Molar and Playwright. Molar autonomously writes and runs critical-path tests, guards production, and clones third parties. Playwright is a library you script and maintain.
- [Molar Trace vs Playwright Trace Viewer | Molar](https://molar.it/vs/playwright-trace) — Compare Molar Trace and Playwright Trace Viewer. Trace adds investigation context, parallel run views, and MCP access alongside Playwright trace artifacts.
- [Molar Clones vs WireMock | Molar](https://molar.it/vs/wiremock) — Compare Molar Clones and WireMock. Clones are vendor-faithful, stateful simulations of Stripe, Twilio, and S3 with signed webhooks and a controlled local runtime. WireMock uses hand-written HTTP stubs that drift.

## Interpretation
The interactive examples on the marketing site are labeled examples or controlled tests. They are not customer testimonials, reliability benchmarks, or guarantees of complete vendor parity. Read the relevant page and documentation before relying on a capability.
